DriverResult<void> Success or DriverError::InvalidParameter
The TLE92466ED's PWM frequency controller is specified to operate between 110 Hz and 4 kHz (datasheet Electrical Characteristics). In period_us terms that is a usable range of:

listitem.para: Standard range (LOW_FREQ_RANGE_EN = 0): 250 µs ≤ period_us ≤ 9090 µs (= 4 kHz .. 110 Hz)
Low-frequency range (LOW_FREQ_RANGE_EN = 1): 2000 µs ≤ period_us ≤ 72727 µs (= 500 Hz .. 13.75 Hz)

detaileddescription.para: The driver auto-selects the appropriate range. Periods outside the combined min/max (250 µs – 72.7 ms) return InvalidParameter. Periods that fall in the gap between the two ranges (9.1 – 2 ms, i.e. 110 Hz – 500 Hz) are accepted but logged as a warning since the PWM-control loop is not specified there.
Formulas: T_pwm = PERIOD_MANT × 2^PERIOD_EXP × (1/f_sys) Low-range: T_pwm = PERIOD_MANT × 8 × 2^PERIOD_EXP × (1/f_sys) f_sys ≈ 8 MHz

simplesect.para: Reaching the ultrasonic range (>20 kHz) is not possible with this chip family — 4 kHz is the hardware ceiling.
This is the recommended API for most users. Use ConfigurePwmPeriodRaw() only if you need direct control over register values.

briefdescription.para: Configure the per-channel dither reference clock (DITHER_CLK_DIV).

detaileddescription.para: Per datasheet §5.3.3.7, DITHER_CLK_DIV (offset 0x0004 within each channel bank) sets the dither reference clock used by both the dither generator and the averaged-feedback engine: tref_clk = MANT × 2^EXP / fSYS POR reset value is 0x0000 which makes tref_clk = 0, the dither period TDither = 0, and (in ICC mode) the measurement period Tmeas = TDither = 0 — so FB_DC / FB_I_AVG / FB_VBAT NEVER update. The high-level ConfigureDither() API calls this function automatically with values derived from the requested dither frequency. Use this API directly if you need a specific tref_clk (e.g. to control the FB update rate independently from the dither amplitude/period).

parameterdescription.para: Desired reference clock period in microseconds. The driver picks the closest representable MANT/EXP and logs the actual value used. Must be > 0; minimum 0.125 µs (1/fSYS).

detaileddescription.para:
Workflow (datasheet §4.10.5):
Freeze feedback for this channel (FB_FRZ).
Poll FB_UPD for the update bit for this channel.
Read FB_DC / FB_VBAT / FB_I_AVG / FB_IMIN_IMAX / FB_PERIOD_MIN_MAX / FB_INT_THRESH.
Release the freeze.

detaileddescription.para: Reads the per-channel FB_I_AVG_s16 register (offset 0x0204) and decodes the 17-bit signed field via FB_I_AVG_s16::ToMilliamps(). This path is distinct from GetAverageCurrent(), which uses the compressed FB_I_AVG mantissa ratio with TP_MANT from FB_DC.

FB_I_AVG_s16 is intended for calibration workflows. The datasheet notes the frame may not be valid while the channel is still settling, so this returns DriverError::FeedbackNotReady when the register still holds the mid-scale placeholder (FB_I_AVG_s16::IsSettlingFrame).

That placeholder check is the only validity gate here. Unlike GetAverageCurrent() this accessor does not confirm the channel has an established measurement window, so prefer GetAverageCurrent() for control and telemetry and keep this one for calibration.

detaileddescription.para: One central 16-bit read covers all six channels (datasheet §5.3.2.10). This is the chip's own "is the data fresh" signal and the first step of the Figure 22 readout; polling it beats guessing at Tmeas with a wall clock, and it costs one register access for the whole device.

briefdescription.para: Set FB_FRZ to channel_mask (bit N freezes channel N).

simplesect.para: Freezing holds FB_DC, FB_VBAT, FB_I_AVG, FB_PERIOD_MIN_MAX and FB_IMIN_IMAX. FB_I_AVG_s16 is free-running and unaffected (§4.10.5).

briefdescription.para: Clear FB_FRZ for every channel, resuming feedback updates.

simplesect.para: Also clears the corresponding FB_UPD bits (§4.10.5).

briefdescription.para: Average current for several channels in one pipelined burst.

detaileddescription.para:
channel_mask
Bit N requests channel N (bits above 5 ignored).
Batch with per-channel current and the masks describing what was actually usable. Never blocks and never polls.
Figure 22 wants a freeze around the FB_DC / FB_I_AVG pair. On the desk Mid eval FB_FRZ is unreadable (and an un-acked freeze sticks, aborting Tmeas for the rest of the session). This path therefore:
writes FB_FRZ=0 (clear a stuck freeze),
reads FB_UPD for telemetry only,
one anchored pipelined burst (ICVID / FB_I_AVG / FB_DC per channel) for every requested channel; TP_MANT gates decode,
writes FB_FRZ=0 again.
A chain whose ICVID anchors do not verify is discarded whole — a spliced neighbour current is never published as this channel's. Host: tests/host/test_tle_anchored_chain.cpp.

simplesect.para: Unlike ReadChannelFeedback this does not wait for FB_UPD. It is meant to be called at the control-loop rate: whatever is ready is sampled, the rest is picked up next tick. That is what makes it usable from a 2 ms thread that also owns actuator writes.

briefdescription.para: Latched error bits for all six channels.

detaileddescription.para: DIAG_ERR_CHGR0..2 each cover a channel pair, so this is one pipelined burst of three reads for the whole device.

simplesect.para: Do not merge this into the same chain as the 22-bit feedback registers. These are 16-bit replies; interleaving widths in one pipeline desynchronised the reply slots on the bench and left every isolated coil misclassified.

briefdescription.para: True when DITHER_CLK_DIV encodes a running measurement clock.

detaileddescription.para: The POR value is 0, which makes tref_clk — and therefore Tmeas — zero, so FB_DC / FB_I_AVG / FB_VBAT never update. Confirming this before trusting feedback is a chip invariant, not caller policy.

This is the primary driver class that provides complete control over the TLE92466ED IC. It manages SPI communication (32-bit with CRC), configuration, current control, monitoring, and diagnostics for all six output channels.
Thread Safety: This class is NOT thread-safe by default. External synchronization is required for multi-threaded access.
Resource Management: Uses RAII principles - init() must be called explicitly but cleanup is automatic.
Error Handling: Uses std::expected for robust error handling without exceptions.
